3:Earshot is an open-source web video player and Chrome extension. They add real-time captions and an interactive transcript to online video using **Deepgram Nova-3** streaming speech-to-text. They don't depend on the video platform's own captions.
4-
5-- **Web platform** (`apps/web`, Next.js): paste a YouTube video or livestream URL and watch it with live captions, plus a searchable transcript with timestamps you can download and click to jump in the video.
6:- **Chrome extension** (`apps/extension`, WXT, Manifest V3): caption whatever is playing in the current tab. It adds a caption box you can drag and resize, and a transcript side panel.
7-
8-Both share one transcription core and one set of UI components (`packages/shared`). YouTube is the first provider, but capture and transcription have no YouTube-specific code.
9-
--
25:├── apps/extension/         # WXT Chrome extension (background, offscreen, overlay, panel, popup)
26-└── docs/provider-policies.md
27-```
28-
--
44:  - **Server key:** if `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` is set on the Next.js server, browsers get a 60-second JWT from `POST /api/deepgram/token`. It's used only to open the WebSocket, and every reconnect fetches a new one. The extension calls the same endpoint; CORS allows `chrome-extension://` origins, optionally limited to listed IDs, and there's a per-IP rate limit. **The server key pays for every visitor.**
45:  - **Bring your own key:** if the server has no key (or a user chooses to), the user pastes their own Deepgram API key. It's stored only in their browser (localStorage, or `chrome.storage.local` in the extension) and sent only to Deepgram, as the WebSocket's `token` subprotocol. Each user pays for their own usage. With a key saved, the extension works on its own, with no Earshot server.
46-- **Interim vs. final results:** interim results update the caption as people speak. Final results are added to a line, and a line is committed when Deepgram detects end of speech (`speech_final` / `UtteranceEnd`). Long continuous speech is split at sentence boundaries so lines stay readable.
47-- **No duplicate segments:** word timestamps are tracked on one timeline across reconnects. Words that were already finalized are dropped when audio is replayed or re-finalized.
48-- **Reliability:** if the connection drops, audio is buffered (last 15 s). The app reconnects with exponential backoff and a fresh token, and reconnects right away when the browser comes back online. KeepAlive messages are sent during silence. Stopping sends `CloseStream` and waits for the final words before closing everything.
--
68:| `EARSHOT_EXTENSION_IDS` | `apps/web/.env.local` | Optional comma-separated extension IDs allowed to request tokens. Unset = any `chrome-extension://` origin (convenient for unpacked builds; set it in production). |
69-| `EARSHOT_TOKEN_RATE_LIMIT` | `apps/web/.env.local` | Optional token requests per IP per minute (default 30). |
70:| `WXT_EARSHOT_URL` | env when building the extension | Earshot server the extension talks to (default `http://localhost:3100`). It can also be changed later in the side panel. |

72-### Run the web platform
73-
--
82:**Don't set `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` on a public deployment** unless you mean to pay for every visitor's captions. The token endpoint has no sign-in, so anyone who opens the site can spend your key's credit (they never see the key itself). Without it, each visitor is asked for their own free Deepgram key the first time they press Start. If you do host a key on purpose, set `EARSHOT_EXTENSION_IDS` and add real authentication or quotas. These rules are also in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for AI coding agents.
83-
84:### Build and load the Chrome extension
85-
86-```bash
87:npm run build -w @earshot/extension
88-```
89-
90:1. Open `chrome://extensions` and turn on **Developer mode**.
91:2. Click **Load unpacked** and select `apps/extension/.output/chrome-mv3`.
92:3. Open the side panel's **Settings** and paste your Deepgram key. (Or skip this and keep the web app running with a server key; the extension then gets tokens from it.)
93-4. Open a YouTube video, click the Earshot toolbar icon, and turn **AI captions** on.
94-
95:For hot reload during development use `npm run dev:extension`. See [apps/extension/README.md](apps/extension/README.md) for the manual test checklist, permissions rationale and more detail.
96-
97-## Testing
98-
--
108:- Audio is captured only after you click Start and pick the tab in the browser's own prompt (web), or click the extension. While captions are on, the web app shows a status badge and the extension shows a `LIVE` toolbar badge.
109-- Audio goes straight from your browser to Deepgram. The Earshot server only issues tokens and never sees audio, text, or a user's own key.
110:- A user's own key is stored in their browser. Anything that can read that browser storage (a malicious extension, or a script injected into the page) could read it too, so the key forms suggest a dedicated key with minimal permissions and an expiry, and offer **Forget key**.
111-- Transcripts stay in memory and are never stored. Only caption appearance settings are saved (localStorage / `chrome.storage.local`). Copy or download a transcript if you want to keep it.
112:- The extension asks only for `tabCapture`, `offscreen`, `sidePanel`, `storage`, `activeTab`, `scripting`. It has no host permissions and no content scripts that run on every page.
113-
114-## Provider policies
115-
--
122:- **Embedding:** videos whose owners disable embedding (YouTube errors 101/150) can't play on the web platform; use the extension on youtube.com instead. `youtube.com/@handle/live` links can't be resolved without the YouTube Data API, so paste the video link.
123:- **Extension:**
124:  - Chrome only allows capture after you click the extension on that tab, so starting from the side panel may need one toolbar click first.
125-  - One tab at a time.
126-  - DRM-protected players capture as silence.
127-  - Timestamps count from when capture started, not video time.
--
130:  - The extension's caption box in fullscreen video and recovery after the service worker is suspended. Both are in the extension's manual checklist.
131-  - Real-audio tests need a visible (headful) Chrome, because headless Chrome captures silent tab audio.
132-- **Token rate limiting** is in memory, per server process. Use a shared store if you run several instances.
133-- **Checking a pasted key:** Deepgram's REST API doesn't accept browser requests, so "Verify & save" checks a key by briefly opening a streaming connection. If a firewall or outage blocks Deepgram, that looks the same as a rejected key.

content.text:
You don't need the Vercel site to use the extension. The extension only contacts an Earshot server to get a temporary Deepgram token, and that only works if the server has `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` set. Your Vercel deployment shouldn't have that key, so there's nothing for the extension to get from it. Use your own key in the extension instead:

1. Build it:
   ```bash
   npm run build -w @earshot/extension
   ```
2. Open `chrome://extensions`, turn on **Developer mode**, click **Load unpacked**, and pick `apps/extension/.output/chrome-mv3`.
3. Click the Earshot toolbar icon, open the side panel's **Settings**, paste your Deepgram API key and click **Verify & save**. The key stays in `chrome.storage.local` and is sent only to Deepgram.
4. Open a YouTube video, click the Earshot toolbar icon on that tab, and turn **AI captions** on. Chrome only allows audio capture after you click the extension on that tab.

**About the "Earshot server URL" setting:** it's only used to get tokens. Once you've saved your own key, you can leave it as is. If you change it to your Vercel URL, the extension will see that the server has no key and ask for yours anyway.

**For other people:** Vercel only hosts the web player. Anyone who wants the extension has to load it unpacked the same way (or you publish it to the Chrome Web Store), and each person adds their own Deepgram key.
